question: Can I Manage WooCommerce Subscriptions From the Command Line With WP-CLI?
metaDescription: WooCommerce Subscriptions doesn't ship its own WP-CLI commands, but subscriptions are fully scriptable through WP-CLI's general WooCommerce/post commands.
shortAnswer: There's no dedicated wp subscription command set built into the plugin, but since a subscription is a WooCommerce order type under the hood, it's fully reachable through WP-CLI's general WooCommerce and post commands, and through custom WP-CLI commands built using the plugin's own PHP functions — useful for bulk operations, scripted migrations, or scheduled maintenance tasks run outside the WordPress admin.

bodyHtml:
How It Works

WP-CLI's generic wp post list --post_type=shop_subscription (on legacy order storage) can list subscriptions the same way it would any custom post type, and WooCommerce's own WP-CLI commands (wp wc) cover core order operations that apply to subscriptions too. For anything more specific — bulk-cancelling subscriptions matching a condition, or triggering a manual renewal from a script — a small custom WP-CLI command wrapping WooCommerce Subscriptions' own PHP functions (wcs_get_subscription() and related) is the practical approach.

// A minimal custom WP-CLI command sketch, registered in a small
// site-specific plugin — not something WooCommerce Subscriptions ships.
WP_CLI::add_command( 'subscriptions cancel-expired-trials', function() {
    $subscriptions = wcs_get_subscriptions( [ 'subscription_status' => 'active' ] );
    foreach ( $subscriptions as $subscription ) {
        if ( $subscription->get_time( 'trial_end' ) < time() && ! $subscription->get_time( 'last_order_date_paid' ) ) {
            $subscription->update_status( 'cancelled' );
        }
    }
} );

What This Is Actually Useful For

  • Bulk maintenance tasks too specific for the admin's built-in bulk actions, run as a one-off script rather than clicking through hundreds of records manually.
  • Scheduled jobs outside of Action Scheduler, for logic that makes more sense as a server cron job calling a WP-CLI command directly than as a WordPress-scheduled action.
  • Data migrations or one-time cleanups, particularly ones needing careful, scriptable, repeatable execution against a staging copy before running on production.
  • CI/CD or deployment automation that needs to interact with subscription data as part of a broader scripted process.

Getting Started Safely

  1. Always test custom WP-CLI commands touching subscription data on a staging copy first, especially anything that changes status or triggers a payment.
  2. Use WooCommerce Subscriptions' own functions rather than raw database queries, for the same forward-compatibility reasons covered in the database-storage question (particularly around HPOS).
  3. Log what a bulk script actually did, not just that it ran successfully, so any unexpected side effect can be traced afterward.

Need a custom WP-CLI command built and tested safely for a specific bulk operation? See custom WooCommerce development.
